title: After the show with Jordan
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Walking home from a concert, Alex and Jordan talk about the band's setlist and new album, build a running playlist with different tempos for easy and long runs, then come back to the concert.

utterances.text: My ears are still ringing. That was so good.
I didn't think the Harbor Kites would be that loud live. The record is so mellow.
Right? And opening with the title track off the new album, Night Ferry, was bold.
I loved it. Everyone expected an old hit and they just started with this slow synth thing.
I wasn't sure about the new album at first, honestly. It's way less guitar.
Same. But hearing it live, the drums are huge. It makes sense in a big room.
And then they played Saltwater third, which is my song.
You screamed. A man in front of us turned around.
Worth it. Okay, but you know what that drummer made me think of? Running.
Oh no. Here we go.
Seriously! You should make a real running playlist. For your half marathon training.
I just put my liked songs on shuffle.
That's why your easy runs aren't easy. A fast song comes on and you sprint.
Okay, true. So what do I do?
Two playlists. For easy runs, slower stuff, around a hundred and fifty beats per minute. Nothing that makes you want to race.
So, like, the mellow Harbor Kites songs.
Exactly. And for the long run, keep it steady. Not faster, just consistent, so you lock into a rhythm for ninety minutes.
What about the end of the long run, when I'm dying?
Save two or three big songs for the last couple of kilometers. Saltwater goes there.
Of course it does. Should I check the tempo for every song?
There are apps that show the BPM. But mostly just notice if a song makes you speed up.
Okay. Easy playlist, long-run playlist, emergency songs at the end. I'll make them tomorrow.
Send them to me. I'll judge them.
Anyway, back to the show. What was that encore?
The acoustic one? I think it's not even released yet.
The singer said it was about her grandmother's boat. The whole room went quiet.
That was my favorite moment. Two thousand people silent.
And then they slammed straight into the loudest song of the night.
Best setlist I've seen in years. We have to go when they tour again.
Deal. Earplugs next time, though.
